title: Traveling with Friends? Expect to Fight over Costs!
paragraphs: It's the last day of your vacation with some friends. You split all the costs between you — well, except that night Penny forgot her purse and everyone had to cover her dinner. And that time Jessica really wanted to go paragliding and you lent her some money.

A survey by travel payment company YouTrip asked 1,000 Singaporeans about their experiences of traveling in groups. It found that one in three had argued with friends over travel expenses. And one in five said they wouldn't travel with the same group again.

According to the survey, waiting a long time to get money back was the most common reason for these problems. Mistakes with the numbers and disagreements about how to split costs fairly were also common.
And the bigger the group, the more difficult things became. Groups of six or more were 1.5 times more likely to have problems with shared costs than people traveling in pairs.
Often, one person ends up paying for things first and keeping track of what everyone owes. YouTrip calls these people the group's "accountant."
But one in three of these "accountants" said they didn't really want the role.

For these reluctant accountants, one of the hardest parts was asking friends to pay them back. Sending reminders was the biggest thing they hated — though getting these messages didn't really bother the people who received them.
And the work doesn't always end when the holiday does. In fact, 45% of reluctant accountants spent more than a day working out who owed what after they got home.
So while traveling with friends can create great memories, sorting out the money may be one part of the trip most people would rather forget!
